paragraphs: Chapter 1045
Episode 249. The First Deployment of the Plutonian (12)
Vahn cannot attack him.
The reason Bligiet was so sure of this was because he thought of her as part of the 'Sun God'.
So, for Vahn to extend her sword to Bligiet was like seawater harming the sea. It was something that couldn't have meaning.
Vahn had precisely understood that thought.
"You may have a great rank comparable to that of Solderet or the witches, but you are not like them. And though you keep telling me that I am blessed by the Sun God, I am not one of you."
Tsz-tsz-tsz-!
A transparent wall unfolded in front of Bligiet. The sword energy Vahn shot for the second time scattered against this wall.
It was the sword of Vahn, a Battle God. A protective shield that perfectly neutralized that sword energy had deployed instantly without any warning.
As soon as he confirmed Bligiet's ability, Vahn smiled satisfactorily.
"Now, we will have a fight worthy of the name."
Understanding the information and objectives of Bligiet, who appeared out of nowhere, was of foremost importance at the alliance level. After all, he had declared himself to be the Sun God.
But from Vahn's personal perspective, Bligiet was an exciting enemy. Unlike Nirgand or Luke, he could satisfy the hunger of a Battle God.
Even the heart-wrenching pain seemed to amplify her fighting spirit.
‘Are you enjoying this, mortal... enduring such pain?’
For Bligiet, it was a series of shocks. The ancient mortals he remembered could not withstand the pressure of the sun energy.
‘My rank may be imperfect, but it's hard to understand the world I created... Of course, I can't solve the constraints left by this insect with my power alone now.’

Bligiet retrieved the lower body of Airen that had fallen to the ground. Blue light waves kept pounding the shield, but Bligiet flicked his finger leisurely. The cut at Airan's waist spread with sun energy, and the lower body attached itself.
"Ever since I first learned about the existence of the Sun God, I've often wondered. Whether my sword could cut through it."
[You can't cut through it. It's just a mistake on your part because my rank has fallen.]
"If I can't cut you, it's an excellent motivation, and if I can, it's a reasonably good practice."
Once again, the Sword of the Plutonian was beginning its assault.

Following the opening, Vahn unfolded the second chapter of the Battle God's technique faster than ever. The sky of the void was covered with thunder, and the ground vibrated heavily with each step she took.
The march of the Battle Gods resounded.
The pleasure of meeting a mighty enemy, the desire to trample on that enemy as always, the confidence of being able to break such a lofty divine status with just a sword.
All her will turned into a blue madness, unleashing countless bolts of lightning.
It depicts the one who reigns above the Plutonian. Only she, the Battle Goddess Vahn, could do so.
"I am the Battle God of the great Plutonian. It's not sudden tales like the blessing of the Sun God that can compel me, but only my hunger for the enemy and the voices of my brothers."
Her voice, like a whirlwind, shook Bligiet's shield.
And before the vibration ceased, the Battle God's sword had already torn through the wall and was flying towards Bligiet's face.
The only one, and the dead.
A god with the face of a friend, hair just like his, a posture like his, eyes like his.
In the thick madness of the joy of battle, rage surged. At the moment the sword touched the god, Vahn refined and refined his anger.
She sharpened it to a single point of the sword tip.
Bligiet couldn't feel that speed. He couldn't see the pale blade with his eyes, nor hear the ear-splitting sound.
Yet, he could avoid it, simply because his divinity was high.
‘I... avoided it?’
Blood splattered from his forehead.
Belatedly looking at where Vahn had charged, Bligiet reflexively took a stance with his sword. This time, it wasn't the divinity reacting but the memory of the flesh.
‘Was I afraid of a mortal's sword?’
His heart seemed to lurch. The fact that he had been dominated by fear for a moment brought an indescribable sense of humiliation.
[How dare you. You are but a fragment of me. I, who created this world.]
As Bligiet shouted, the madness filling the void disappeared as if it were a lie.
But it was only for a moment. In the time it took for an eyelid to close and open, the madness surrounded Bligiet again.
She was charging at a being who claimed to be the god of gods. The protective shield, melting away like foam, Bligiet had to choose.
He had no choice but to move like a mortal. He had to raise the sun's energy, emit the will to block the madness, spread his powers, he couldn't shake off the persistent madness just with that.
He twisted his body as the flesh remembered, stepped on the footwork, touched the ground, and rolled on the floor. Ash, dirt, the flesh and blood of the convicts soiled Bligiet's body.
Airan was annoying.
It seemed that if he just threw away the flesh clutched in his right hand, he could have evaded more easily. The urge to do so was throbbing in his head.
"You are also just one of the fragments of the Sun God, Bligiet. If you were such an almighty being, you would have already taken my breath away."
[I shall grant you that.]
Bligiet threw Airan away and reached out his hand.
After all, the body of Airan, no matter how much it was torn, could be reattached. It was just unpleasant to change his attitude while dealing with mortals.
Then, as Bligiet clenched his fist, suddenly Vahn stopped abruptly and spat out blood.
"Kahak!"
The sun energy accumulated in the heart was exploding. It felt like Bligiet's hand was directly entering into the heart and rummaging through it.
He thought he had her life in his hands.
That's what Bligiet thought. And before even 5 seconds passed, he had to reflect on his endless arrogance.
‘It doesn't shatter...!’
No matter how hard he clenched his fist, no matter how much sun energy he emitted.

Vahn's heart, caught in his power, showed no signs of destruction. Instead, the more he clenched, the harder it became and soon, Vahn was approaching him steadily. She wasn't even screaming in pain anymore, nor flinching.
"Keuk... I'll kill you..."
Bligiet concentrated his mind. Like when Vahn first tried to figure him out.
‘A life so short and finite to perceive a thousand years as a long time, yet a power that seems to reach eternity... That's a great contradiction.’
Looking again, Vahn had a lot in common with his current self. Even he, the beginning and end of the world, the very creation itself, was bound by the flesh of Temar and the constraints of Airan.
‘A flaw that will certainly be erased once the world is complete, but it's pitiful and beautiful nature cannot be denied. That's why the original me must have struggled.’
Eventually, Bligiet decided to classify Vahn as 'equal' to his current self.
Since he had barely revived through the flesh and left arm remaining from the radiant mortal collected by the Sun God Religion, it was an inevitable choice.
[Vahn, you make me realize the reason for my existence, to my imperfection.]
Bligiet withdrew his hand.
He was a being who, unless he was as complete as in the beginning, could not take life with his power. Only one who could fight and win against him could kill him.
"All I want to hear from your mouth are screams and cries."
Sssht, chrueng-!
Vahn and Bligiet's swords clashed. Both of them were gritting their teeth, pushing each other back. And they knew. That they still had more to offer each other.
Vahn had not yet unfolded the final chapter of her Plutonian Sword Technique, and Bligiet had not made his decision.
Whether to fight to the end with Vahn, accepting annihilation, or to retreat for the time being.
Bligiet couldn't easily choose which was better.

If he lost the fight, resurrection would be far away again, and the world would not be complete. But even if he fought again after raising his divinity, Vahn was not a mortal who could be crushed and killed by his power.
He didn't have much time to ponder.
The madness that had surged like a tidal wave was beginning to subside, a sign that the end of the Plutonian Sword Technique was about to start.

Bligiet was watching the warrior god from half a millennium ago cut down numerous immortals with that sword. Moments when gods, small or great, born from the will of the sun, shattered under the mortal sword, the day when the error of light, called a malevolent spirit in the present world, was overwhelmed.
‘An error with an error. Order cannot rectify Vahn.’
Suddenly such a thought popped into Bligiet's head. It was right after Sigmund grazed his neck. His blade was passing by Vahn's eyes.
Whoosh…!
Bligiet stepped back and waved his hand in the air. Spheres emitting light as if looking directly at the sun appeared, and Vahn stopped his movement, reading his actions.
"Bligiet. Are you thinking of running away?"
[Even for me, fighting to the end with you in a mortal body is an excessive gamble. It's my fault for not refining the world properly, so I'll gladly accept this humiliation.]
Vahn looked up directly at the light. Her pupils had already overcome the burning-like light, but Bligiet was stepping into a golden dimensional gate.
"If you can't kill me now, you'll never be able to kill me And yet, you're saying you'll retreat?"
Airan's body, which had been scattered into six parts, was also reconstituted and caught in Bligiet's hand.
The fight was over. The moment Vahn intuitively sensed that, she hesitated due to unexpected emotions.
More than the anger and competitive spirit towards Bligeit, it was the bitter feeling of losing a friend’s flesh, and not being able to let him rest now, that filled her inside.
"Yeah, maybe you can run away from me forever. But that left arm's... My brother will not let you go like now, Bligiet."
Bligiet did not answer and stepped through the dimensional gate. Thinking that she needed to escape the flesh using Airan and the left arm as soon as possible.
